'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afghanistan conflict (1978–present)|Afghanistan conflict]]
**[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
***[[List of drone strikes in Afghanistan#2021|2021 drone strikes in Afghanistan]]
****[[United States Marine Corps|Marine Corps]] [[General (United States)|General]] [[Kenneth F. McKenzie Jr.]] acknowledges that a [[drone strike]] conducted by the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] on [[August 2021 Kabul drone strike|August 29]] near [[Kabul International Airport]] killed 10 civilians instead of [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant – Khorasan Province|ISIL-K]] militants. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/17/us/politics/pentagon-drone-strike-afghanistan.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Internal conflict in Myanmar]]
**Eighty telecommunication towers owned by [[Mytel]] have been destroyed in [[Myanmar]], leaving 700,000 people without communication. The [[People's Defence Force (Myanmar)|People's Defence Force]] has claimed responsibility for the destruction. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/attacks-myanmar-telecom-towers-show-evolving-tactics-conflict-2185661 (CNA)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Singapore]]
*****[[Prime Minister of Singapore|Prime Minister]] [[Lee Hsien Loong]] receives a [[booster dose]] of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/health/pm-lee-receives-his-covid-19-booster-jab (''The Straits Times'')]
****[[Singapore]] reports 935 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of new cases since April 2020. [https://www.usnews.com/news/world/articles/2021-09-17/singapore-reports-935-new-covid-19-cases-highest-since-april-last-year (''U.S. News and World Report'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]] begins a COVID-19 vaccination rollout for children over the age of 6 using the [[China|Chinese]]-made [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/2183587/cambodia-vaccinating-children-as-young-as-6 (''Bangkok Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
****[[India]] reports a new single-day record of 22.5 million doses of the COVID-19 vaccine administered. [https://www.livemint.com/news/india/india-sets-new-single-day-record-by-administering-1-60-cr-covid-vaccine-doses-11631872671546.html (Livemint)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]], [[COVID-19 drug development]]
****[[South Korea]] approves the [[Celltrion]] antibody COVID-19 treatment for infected adults in high-risk groups and adults with severe symptoms. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/south-korea-approves-celltrions-covid-19-treatment-use-2021-09-17/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in American Samoa]]
****[[American Samoa]] reports its first case of COVID-19 in a resident who returned from travelling to the [[Contiguous United States|U.S. mainland]] and [[Hawaii]] earlier this week. [https://apnews.com/article/health-coronavirus-pandemic-hawaii-honolulu-american-samoa-6433b498bfaf61a7846ad0718c91680b (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] lifts its containment area borders on the main island of [[Viti Levu]] as 60% of the targeted population has been fully [[COVID-19 vaccination in Fiji|vaccinated]]. However, a curfew remains in effect and inter-island travel remains suspended. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/451651/mainland-fiji-border-barriers-lifted (RNZ)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[New Zealand]] extends the suspension of the travel bubble agreement with [[Australia]] for a further eight weeks as the number of COVID-19 cases continues to remain high and also due to the spread of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/17/nz-australia-travel-bubble-suspension-stays-amid-delta-outbreaks (Al Jazeera)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
***The [[Slovenia]]n [[Government of Slovenia|government]] announces that all public sector employees, with the exception of employees working in the education sector, will have to show a proof of [[COVID-19 vaccination in Slovenia|vaccination]] or recovery from COVID-19 beginning on October 1 or they risk losing their jobs. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/slovenia-govt-workers-face-mandatory-jabs-01631879107 (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
***Advisers to the [[Food and Drug Administration]] vote to reject a wider COVID-19 vaccine [[booster dose]] and to only recommend booster doses for people over the age of 65 and people who are at high risk of severe illness. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/09/17/fda-panel-begins-voting-on-pfizers-covid-booster-doses-rejecting-shots-for-general-public.html (CNBC)]
**[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
***A five-month survey finds that the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] is the most effective vaccine against hospitalization due to COVID-19. The study found that Moderna’s vaccine candidate had a 93% effectiveness in reducing hospitalizations, compared to 88% for [[Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer]]’s, and 71% for [[Janssen COVID-19 vaccine|Johnson & Johnson]]’s. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/covid-vaccine-efficacy-study-pfizer-moderna-johnson-and-johnson/ (CBS News)]
*[[2021 Marburg virus disease outbreak in Guinea]]
**[[Guinea]] declares an end to the outbreak of the [[Marburg virus disease]] in the country. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/09/17/africa/guinea-marburg-virus-over-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''International relations'''
*[[AUKUS]]
**The [[Australia]]n [[Minister for Defence (Australia)|Defence Minister]] announces that the new strategic partnership will also include increased numbers of [[United States|U.S.]] bombers and airplanes being based out of [[Australia]]. In addition, the [[Carnegie Endowment for International Peace]] notes that the deal has revealed a loophole in nuclear policy that does not bar states without nuclear weapons from obtaining nuclear technology for submarines and that this falls outside of [[IAEA]] inspections. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-09-17/us-raises-concerns-about-china-economic-coercion-of-australia/100469360 (ABC News Australia)] [https://foreignpolicy.com/2021/09/16/u-s-seeking-basing-in-australia-after-submarine-deal/ (Foreign Policy)]
**[[France]] recalls its ambassadors from the [[United States]] and [[Australia]] in protest of the security pact, which also includes the [[United Kingdom]]. The French Foreign Ministry says that the "exceptional decision" was justified by the seriousness of the pact, which has replaced its own security agreement with Australia. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-58604677 (BBC News)]
*[[Foreign relations of Iran]]
**The [[Shanghai Cooperation Organization]] grants membership status to [[Iran]]. [https://asia.nikkei.com/Politics/International-relations/Iran-to-gain-Central-Asia-clout-with-entry-into-SCO-security-club (Nikkei Asia)]
*[[Libya–Tunisia relations]],  [[Libya–Tunisia border]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Libya]] and [[Tunisia]] reopen their borders with stringent health protocol requiring travellers to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19 and [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] tested negative, two months after the closure on July 8 due to an explosion of [[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia|COVID-19 cases in the latter country]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210917-libya-tunisia-border-reopens-after-covid-closure (AFP via France 24)]
*[[North Korea–United States relations]]
**In escalating tensions over the past week, [[North Korea]] accuses the [[United States]] of double standards when it comes to condemning missile tests, saying that the U.S. only condemned North Korea the same day that [[South Korea]] also tested missiles. North Korean state media cited its chief as saying that the American response was a "vivid revelation of the American-style double-dealing attitude" and also says that unless "the U.S. drops its hostile policies towards North Korea, denuclearization can never be put on the table" of negotiations. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/nkorea-accuses-us-double-standards-missiles-hampering-talks-2021-09-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[Djibouti–Somalia relations]]
**Somali president [[Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed]] condemns [[Djibouti]] for detaining and forbidding a Somali security advisor from leaving the country. The president accused Djibouti of "destabilizing" relations amid a political feud between the Somali president and prime minister. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/somalias-president-berates-djibouti-detaining-his-security-adviser-2021-09-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[Ukraine–United States relations]]
**[[Ukraine]] and the [[United States]] announce that they will begin joint military exercises involving 15 other countries in western Ukraine next week. [https://www.voanews.com/a/ukraine-us-to-hold-joint-military-drills-/6232331.html (VOA)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*Aftermath of the [[2021 Argentine legislative election]]
**[[President of Argentina|President]] [[Alberto Fernández]] reshuffles his cabinet, as demanded by [[Vice President of Argentina|Vice President]] [[Cristina Fernández de Kirchner]], following the poor turnout of their [[Peronism|Peronist]] and [[Kirchnerism|Kirchnerist]] [[Frente de Todos]] coalition in the legislative [[Primary elections in Argentina|primary election]]. Among the appointed ministers include [[Santiago Cafiero]], [[Julián Domínguez]], [[Aníbal Fernández]], and [[Daniel Filmus]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/argentina-s-president-reshuffles-cabinet-after-political-crisis-official (AFP via Radio France Internationale)]
*[[Ank Bijleveld]], the [[List of Ministers of Defence of the Netherlands|Minister of Defence of the Netherlands]], resigns following a [[Motion of no confidence|motion of censure]] for her handling of the Dutch evacuation during the [[Fall of Kabul (2021)|Fall of Kabul]], a day after the resignation of [[Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Netherlands|Minister of Foreign Affairs]] [[Sigrid Kaag]]. [https://nos.nl/artikel/2398138-na-kaag-d66-treedt-ook-minister-bijleveld-cda-af-ik-sta-werk-defensie-in-de-weg (NOS)] [https://www.rfi.fr/en/second-dutch-minister-quits-as-afghan-scandal-widens (Radio France Internationale)]
*[[President of El Salvador|President]] of [[El Salvador]] [[Nayib Bukele]] says that the proposed constitutional reforms he sent for review will not include the legalization of abortion or [[same-sex marriage]]. El Salvador has one of the strictest anti-abortion laws in the world. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/salvadoran-president-rules-out-allowing-abortion-same-sex-marriage-2021-09-17/ (Reuters)]
